--- ## Walkthrough The changes extract the `ProviderMetadata` struct and related constants from the `providerimages` package into a new dedicated `providermetadata` package under `manifests-gen`. The root `go.mod` adds a local `manifests-gen` requirement with a `replace` to `./manifests-gen`. Imports and usages are updated to reference the new package. ## Changes |Cohort / File(s)|Summary| |---|---| |**Root module update**
`go.mod`|Added `require` for `github.com/openshift/cluster-capi-operator/manifests-gen` and a `replace` directive mapping that module path to `./manifests-gen`.| |**manifests-gen module files**
`manifests-gen/go.mod`, `manifests-gen/generate.go`|`manifests-gen/go.mod` adjusted indirect dependencies (removed several docker/estargz/logrus-related entries; added testing and monitoring/tooling deps). `generate.go` now constructs metadata using `providermetadata.ProviderMetadata` and imports the new package.| |**New providermetadata package**
`manifests-gen/providermetadata/metadata.go`|Added new package `providermetadata` with exported `ProviderMetadata` struct (JSON tags for name, attributes, ocpPlatform, selfImageRef, installOrder), constants `AttributeKeyType` and `AttributeKeyVersion`, and method `MatchesPlatform`.| |**Provider images refactor**
`pkg/providerimages/providerimages.go`|Replaced local `ProviderMetadata` definition with type alias `type ProviderMetadata = providermetadata.ProviderMetadata` and sourced `AttributeKeyType`/`AttributeKeyVersion` from the new package.| ## Estimated code review effort 🎯 3 (Moderate) | ⏱️ ~22 minutes

<details>

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-capi-operator/pull/503):

>Move ProviderMetadata, MatchesPlatform, and attribute key constants into manifests-gen/providermetadata/ so both the metadata producer (manifests-gen) and consumer (pkg/providerimages) share one canonical type definition.
>
>This dependency reversal allows manifests-gen to be imported externally. This shifts the import issue into cluster-capi-operator where it is not an issue as there is nothing importing it.
>
>Alternatives:
>- Add third go.mod for just this struct. Both manifests-gen and cluster-api-operator would import this. Disadvantage of this approach is that it would require two-step update processes. First update the struct and publish it. Then update the consumers.
>- Keep as is and use real version of go.mod in manifests-gen go.mod. This has the same issue of two-step updates of the struct.
>- Remove manifests-gen go.mod. Disadvantage is that this would combine the dependency graph.
